<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{bijfra-1}
Let $G$ be a semi-abelian $\pi$-formal group scheme of relative dimension $g$ 
over $S$. 
Then the operator $\fra^*: {\bf H}_\delta(G)_K \rightarrow {\bf H}_\delta(G)_K$ is a 
bijection.

Hence $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}({\bf H}_\delta(G)_K)$ is a non-degenerate filtered isocrystal.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{isoupsemi-1}
Let $G$ be a semi-abelian $\pi$-formal group scheme of relative 
dimension $g$ over $S$. 
Then the  $R$-linear map $\Upsilon: \bXp(G) \rightarrow (\operatorname{\mathrm{Lie}} G)^*$ is an 
injective morphism of $R$-modules that has $\pi$-power torsion cokernel.

In particular, $\Upsilon_K: \bXp(G)_K \rightarrow (\operatorname{\mathrm{Lie}} G)^*_K$ is an isomorphism
of $K$-vector spaces.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{Iso-crys-11}
Let $A$ be an elliptic curve over $S$. 
                                    
                                                                    
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A$ is a non-CL elliptic curve then
$$
\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}} (\Hd(A)_{K}) \simeq \mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}} (\Hcr(A)_{K})
$$
in the category of filtered isocrystals.


\item  If $A$ has CL then $$\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}} (\Hd(A)_{K}) \simeq 
\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}} (H^0(A, \Omega_A)_{K})$$ 
in the category of filtered isocrystals 
where $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}} (H^0(A,\Omega_A)_{K})$
is the one dimensional sub-object of $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(\Hcr(A)_{K})$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
For all $n \geq 0$, there exists a unique functorial $R$-algebra 
structure on $W_n(B)$ such that $w$ is a natural transformation of 
functors of $R$-algebras.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{NandJ}
Let $G$ be a $\pi$-formal group scheme over $S$. Then
$$
N^*G \simeq J^*(N^1G),
$$
as a canonical isomorphism of prolongation sequences of $\pi$-formal schemes 
over $S^*$. In particular, for all $n \geq 1$ we have
$$
N^nG \simeq J^{n-1}G.
$$
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{NandJphi}
For all $n \geq 2$ we have the following commutative diagram of $\pi$-formal 
group schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
J^{n-1}(N^1G) \simeq N^nG \ar[r]^-{\phi \circ \iota} \ar[d]_\fra & J^{n-1}G 
\ar[d]^\phi \\
J^{n-2}(N^1G) \simeq N^{n-1}G \ar[r]^-{\phi \circ \iota} & J^{n-2}G.
}
$$
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{comfact}
Let $G$ be a smooth group scheme over $S$. Then
the morphism of group schemes 
$(\phi \circ \iota - \iota \circ \fra) : N^nG \rightarrow J^{n-1}G$ uniquely factors through  $N^1G$ as
$$\xymatrix{
N^nG \ar[rr]^-{\phi \circ \iota - \iota \circ \fra}  
\ar[d]_u & & J^{n-1}G \\
N^1G \ar[rru]_\Delta & &
}$$
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
See Theorem $4.4$ in \cite{BS_b}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{diff}
Let $\Theta$ be a delta character in ${\bf X}_n(G)$.
\begin{enumerate}
        \item We have
                $$
                \iota^*\phi^*\Theta = \mathfrak{f}^*(\iota^*\Theta)+ 
\gamma_\Theta. \Psi_1,
                $$
                where $\gamma_\Theta=\pi A_0$. 
        \item For $n\geq 2$, we have
                $$
                \iota^*(\phi^{\circ n})^*\Theta= (\mathfrak{f}^{n-1})^* \iota^*\phi^*\Theta.
                $$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
See Proposition $6.3$ in \cite{BS_b}
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{Nniso}
Let $f:U \rightarrow V$ be an \'{e}tale morphism of pointed affine $\pi$-formal 
schemes. Then
$N^n U \simeq N^nV$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Let $U = \operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}} A$ and $V= \operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}} B$. Then $J^nU \simeq J^nV \times_V U \simeq
J_nB \hat{\otimes}_B A$. Then
\begin{eqnarray*}
N^nU & \simeq & J^nU \times_U S \\
&=& \operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}}~ (J_nB \hat{\otimes}_B A \hat{\otimes}_A R) \\
&=& \operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}}~ (J_nB \hat{\otimes}_B R) \\
& =& N^nV.
\end{eqnarray*}
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{equalpi}
Let $f:U \rightarrow V$ be an \'{e}tale morphism of pointed affine $\pi$-formal 
schemes. Then $U(\pi) = V(\pi) $.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $U= \operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}} A$ and $V=\operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}} B$ and $U(\pi) \rightarrow V(\pi)$ be the natural map 
between functors. Let $g \in (V(\pi))(C/\pi^n C)$ for any $\pi$-adically 
complete $R$-algebra. Then we have
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[d]_-f & \operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}} (C/\pi C) \ar[l]_-{\bar{e}} \ar@{^{(}_->}[d] \\
V & \operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}} (C/\pi^n C) \ar[l]^-g
}
$$
Since $f:U \rightarrow V$ is \'{e}tale, $g$ has a unique lift $h: \operatorname{\mathrm{Spec}}(C/\pi^n C)
\rightarrow U$ making the above diagram commutative for all $n \geq 1$. Since $C$
is $\pi$-adically complete, this proves our result.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{phiiso}
Let $X$ be a pointed smooth $\pi$-formal $S$-scheme. Then the morphism 
$\phi \circ i$ induces the isomorphism
$$
(\phi\circ i): (N^1X) \simeq X(\pi). 
$$
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Since $X$ is smooth over $S$, there exists an affine open subscheme $U\subset
X$ containing $e$ such that there exists an \'{e}tale morphism $f:U \rightarrow V$ 
such that $V = \operatorname{\mathrm{Spf}} R[\bx]\hat{\ }$, where
$\bx=(x_1,\dots, x_d)$ and $d$ is the relative dimension of $X$ over $S$.
Note that $N^1X \simeq N^1U$ and $X(\pi) \simeq U(\pi)$. By 
Proposition \ref{Nniso} we have $N^1X \simeq N^1V$. Then the result follows 
from (\ref{phipiiso}) and Proposition \ref{equalpi}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{formaliso}
Let $\beta:G \rightarrow G$ be an endomorphism of group schemes and let $\beta: \Gfor
\rightarrow \Gfor$ still denote the induced endomorphism on the associated formal
group law $\Gfor$. Then we have the following commutative diagram of 
formal group laws:
$$\xymatrix{
\Gfor \otimes K \ar[d]_{\log_G} \ar[r]^\beta & \Gfor \otimes K \ar[d]^{\log_G}\\
(\hGa \otimes K)^g \ar[r]^{D\beta} & (\hGa \otimes K)^g.
}$$
In particular we have 
$$
\log_G(\beta(\bx)) = D\beta \log_G (\bx)
$$
for all $\bx \in \Gfor \otimes K$.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Let $\bx$ be a coordinate system around the identity section of $\Gfor$. We
denote by the same $\bx$, the induced coordinate on $TG^{\mathrm{for}}$
giving the isomorphism $TG^{\mathrm{for}} \simeq (\hGa)^g$.

In terms of the coordinate $\bx$, we have
$$
\beta(\bx) = B\bx  \pmod {\bx^2}  
$$
where $B = D \beta$ is the derivative matrix of $\beta$ at the identity section 

Also we have 
\begin{align}
\nonumber\exp_G(\bx) &= \bx \pmod{\bx^2} \\
\nonumber \log_G(\bx) &= \bx \pmod{\bx^2} 
\end{align}
where the above maps are inverses of each other in the category of
formal group laws over $K$. Then consider the composition

\begin{align}
\nonumber
(\hGa \otimes K)^g \stk{\exp_G}{\longrightarrow} \Gfor \otimes K 
\stk{\beta}{\longrightarrow}
 \Gfor \otimes K \stk{\log_G}{\longrightarrow} (\Gfor \otimes K)^g.
\end{align}
We have 
$\gamma(\bx):= \log_G \circ \beta \circ \exp_G (\bx) = B\bx \pmod{\bx^2} $. 
Since $\gamma$ is an endomorphism of $(\hGa)^g$, $\gamma$ must be a linear 
operator. 
Therefore $\gamma (\bx) = B \bx $ and hence we have
\begin{align}
\log_G \circ \beta \circ \exp_G &= D\beta. \nonumber 
\end{align}
Since $\log_G$ and $\exp_G$ are inverses to each other, we obtain
\begin{align}
 \log_G \circ \beta  &= D\beta \circ \log_G \nonumber 
\end{align}
and we are done.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{Frob-char}
Let $\overline{G}$ be a semi-abelian scheme over $\operatorname{\mathrm{Spec}} k$ satisfying the following 
extension of smooth group schemes
$$
0 \rightarrow \overline{T} \stk{f}{\rightarrow} \overline{G} \stk{g}{\rightarrow} \overline{A} \rightarrow 0,
$$
where $\overline{T}$ is a multiplicative torus and $\overline{A}$ is an abelian scheme 
over $\operatorname{\mathrm{Spec}} k$. Then
$$
P({F}_{\bar{G}}) = 0 
$$
where $P(F) = P_{\bar{T}}(F) \circ P_{\bar{A}}(F)$.

In particular, we have 
$$
P(F) = F^{2g+1} + (b_{2g-1}-q)  F^{2g} + \cdots + (q^g-qb_1) F - q^{g+1}.
$$
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Consider the following diagram satisfied by the absolute Frobenius $\bar{F}$
$$\xymatrix{
\overline{G} \ar[d]_{P_{\bar{A}}(\bar{F})} \ar[r]^g & \overline{A} 
\ar[d]^{P_{\bar{A}}(\bar{F})}\\
\overline{G} \ar[r]^g & \overline{A}. 
} $$
For all $x \in \bar{G}$ we have
 $f \circ P_{\bar{A}}(F)(x) = P_{\bar{A}}(F)(f({x})) = 0$. Therefore 
$P_{\bar{A}}(x) \in \mathrm{Image} (f)$. Hence we have 
$P_{\bar{T}}(F)(P_{\bar{A}}(F)(x)) = 0$ and this completes the proof of the first 
part.

The second part follows from the fact that $P_{\bar{T}}(F)= F - q$ and 
$P_{\bar{A}}(F) = F^{2g} + b_{2g-1}F^{2g-1} + \cdots + b_1 F + q^g$ for some 
$b_i \in {\mathbb Z},~ i = 1,\dots , 2g-1$ and $g = \dim \bar{A}$. Then for all $x \in
\overline{G}$ we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
P(F)(x) &=& P_{\bar{T}}(F)(P_{\bar{A}}(F)(x)\\
&=& P_{\bar{T}}(F)
(F^{2g}(x) + b_{2g-1}F^{2g-1}(x) + \cdots + b_1 F(x) + q^g(x))\\
&=& (F - q)
(F^{2g}(x) + b_{2g-1}F^{2g-1}(x) + \cdots + b_1 F(x) + q^g(x))\\
&=&
(F^{2g+1} + (b_{2g-1}-q)F^{2g} + \cdots + (q^g-qb_1)F - q^{g+1})(x)
\end{eqnarray*}
and this proves our result.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{isoupsilon}
Let $G$ be a $\pi$-formal smooth commutative group scheme of finite type 
over $S$ such that the absolute Frobenius $F$ on $\overline{G}$ satisfies $P(F) =0$ where 
$$
P(F) = F^m + b_{m-1} F^{m-1} + \cdots + b_1 F + q^h
$$
for some $h \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$.
             
Then $\Gamma \in \Mat_{g \times g}(K)$ as in (\ref{Gammamatrix}) is invertible.

\color{black}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
For all $j=1,\dots, g$, define the delta character of order $2g$ as 
$\tTheta_j:J^{2g}G \rightarrow \hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}}$ given by
\begin{align}
\tTheta_j:= \mathrm{pr}_j \circ \Psi_1 \circ \mathfrak{g}.
\end{align}
Then by the above diagram we have 
\begin{align}
(\phi \circ \iota)^* f_j = \pr_j \circ \Psi_1 \circ P(\fra).
\end{align}
Note that the morphism $\Psi_1 \circ P(\fra): N^{2g+1}G \rightarrow \hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}}^g$ is given
by 
\begin{align}
\Psi_{m+1}+ b_{m-1}\Psi_{m} + \cdots + q^h \Psi_1.
\end{align}

Hence we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
(\phi \circ \iota)^* \tTheta_j &=& \pr_j \circ (\Psi_1 \circ P(\fra))\\
&=& \pr_j \circ (\Psi_{m+1} + b_{m-1}\Psi_{m}+ \cdots + q^h \Psi_1 )\\
&=& \pr_j \circ (\Psi_{m+1} + b_{m-1}\Psi_{m}+ \cdots b_1\Psi_2) 
+ \pr_j \circ q^h \Psi_1. \\
\end{eqnarray*}
By Proposition \ref{diff} (1), note that 
$$
\fra^* (\iota^* \tTheta) = \pr_j \circ (\Psi_{m+1} + b_{m-1}\Psi_{m}+ 
\cdots b_1\Psi_2).
$$

Therefore we have 
\begin{align}
\label{phi-up2}
\Delta^* \tTheta_j := (\phi \circ \iota - \iota \circ \fra)^*\tTheta_j =
 q^h e_j. \Psi_1
\end{align}
where $e_j$ is the $j$-th row of the $g\times g$ identity matrix 
$\mathbf{1}_{g}$.
On the other hand by (\ref{phiup}), for all $j$ there exists 
$c_{1j},\dots, c_{gj} \in R$ such that
\begin{align}
\label{phi-up3}
\Delta^* \tTheta_j &= (\phi(c_{1j}) \gamma_1 + \cdots + 
\phi(c_{gj}) \gamma_g). \Psi_1
\end{align}
Hence comparing equations (\ref{phi-up2}) and (\ref{phi-up3}) for all $j$ we obtain that 
\begin{align}
\label{phi-up4}
C. \Gamma =  q^h \mathbf{1}_g,
\end{align}
where $C= (\phi(c_{ij}))_{ij} \in \Mat_{g\times g}(R)$. Hence $\Gamma$ is invertible
over $K$ and we are done.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{isoupsemi}
Let $G$ be semi-abelian $\pi$-formal group scheme over $S$ of relative 
dimension $g$. 
Then the  $R$-linear map $\Upsilon: \bXp(G) \rightarrow (\operatorname{\mathrm{Lie}} G)^*$ is an 
injective morphism of $R$-modules with $\pi$-power torsion cokernel.

In particular, $\Upsilon: \bXp(G)_K \rightarrow (\operatorname{\mathrm{Lie}} G)^*_K$ is an isomorphism
of $K$-vector spaces.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
It is sufficient to show that $\Upsilon$ is an isomorphism of 
$K$-vector spaces. By \eqref{Upsilonmatrix}, it is then enough to show 
that $\Gamma$ is an invertible matrix over $K$.
Since $G$ is a semi-abelian scheme of dimension $g$ over $S$, by Proposition
\ref{Frob-char}, the absolute $q$-power Frobenius $F$ on $\overline{G}$ satisfies
the polynomial $P(F)$  in the proposition. 
Hence the result follows from Theorem \ref{isoupsilon}.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{Lambdamu}
For all $n \geq \mup$, we have
$$
{\bf X}_n(G)_K/u^*{\bf X}_{n-1}(G)_K \stk{[\iota^*  \phi^*]}{\longrightarrow}
\mathrm{Hom}(N^{n+1}G,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}})_K/u^*\mathrm{Hom}(N^nG,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}})_K
$$
is an isomorphism. 

In particular, for $n=\mup$, we have 
$$
{\bf X}_{\mup} (G)_K/u^*{\bf X}_{\mup-1}(G)_K \stk{[\iota^*  \phi^*]}{\longrightarrow}
\mathrm{Hom}(N^{{\mup} +1}G,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}})_K/u^*\mathrm{Hom}(N^\mup G,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}})_K
$$
is an isomorphism and hence $\Lambda_{\mup}$ is an invertible matrix over $K$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{bijfra}

If $G$ is a semi-abelian $\pi$-formal scheme of relative dimension $g$ over
$S$, then the operator $\fra^*: {\bf H}_\delta(G)_K \rightarrow 
{\bf H}_\delta(G)_K$ is a bijection 

Hence $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}({\bf H}_\delta(G)_K)$ is a non-degenerate filtered isocrystal.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Since $G$ is a semi-abelian $\pi$-formal scheme over $S$, by Theorem 
\ref{Frob-char} the absolute Frobenius $F$ on $\overline{G}$ satisfies $P(F) = 0$ 
for some $P(t) = t^m + b_{m-1}t^{m-1} + \cdots + b_1 t + q^h \in \mathbb{Z}[t]$.
By equation (\ref{phi-up4}) in the 
proof of Theorem \ref{isoupsilon} we have $\Gamma = 
(\gamma_1 \cdots \gamma_g)^t$ is an invertible $g\times g$ matrix over $K$.
Hence we have 
$$
\det [\fra^*] = (-1)^{\mup} \det (\Lambda_{\mup}^{-1} \Gamma) \ne 0.
$$
Therefore the semilinear map $\fra^*: \mathrm{Hom}(N^{\mup}G,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}})_K \rightarrow 
\mathrm{Hom}(N^{\mup}G,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}})_K$ is bijective. Hence this implies that the map $\fra^*$
on the quotient ${\bf H}_\delta(G)_K$ is also bijective.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{fra-map}
Let $A$ be an elliptic curve over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A$ is not a Frobenius lift, then 
$${\bf H}_{\delta}(A) \simeq R\langle \Psi_1, \Psi_2 \rangle, ~ \bXp(A) \simeq 
R\langle \Theta_2 \rangle.$$ 
The semilinear operator $\fra^*$ acts as 
$$\fra^*(\Psi_1) = \gamma \Psi_2,~ \fra^*(\Psi_2) = \phi(\lambda)\Psi_2 -
\gamma \Psi_1.$$

\item If $A$ is a Frobenius lift, then 
$${\bf H}_{\delta}(A) \simeq R\langle \Psi_1 \rangle, ~ \bXp(A) \simeq 
R\langle \Theta_1 \rangle.$$ 
The semilinear operator $\fra^*$ acts as 
$$\fra^*(\Psi_1) = -\gamma \Psi_1.$$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{char-poln}
Let $A$ be an elliptic curve over $S$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A$ is not a Frobenius lift then $\mathrm{char }~{[\fra^*]}_{\mathbb{B}} = 
t^2 - \phi(\lambda)t + \gamma$

\item If $A$ has a Frobenius lift then $\mathrm{char}~{[\fra^*]}_{\mathbb{B}} = 
t + \gamma$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The result follows directly from Theorem \ref{fra-map}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{theta-lemma}
Let $A/R$ be a non-CL elliptic curve over $S$ and  $P(t) = t^2 - a_q(A)t + q$ 
be the characteristic polynomial satisfied by the absolute  Frobenius 
$\overline{F}$ in $\mathrm{End}(\overline{A})$. Then 
$$
\iota^* \phi^* \Theta_2 = \Psi_3 - a_q(A) \Psi_2 + q \Psi_1.
$$
In particular, we have $\lambda = a_q(A)$ and $\gamma = q$ and 
$$ \mathrm{char}~{[\fra^*]}_{\mathbb{B}} = P(t) = t^2 - a_q(A)t + q. $$
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
For elliptic curve $A$ the diagram (\ref{frob-diag}) turns out to be as follows:
$$
\xymatrix{ 
 N^{3}A \ar[r]^-{\phi\circ \iota} \ar[d]_-{P(\mathfrak{f})} & J^{2}A \ar[r] 
\ar@{.>}[dl]_{\mathfrak{g}} \ar[d]_-{P(\mathfrak{\phi})} & \overline{A} 
\ar[d]_-{P(\overline{F})} \\
 N^1A\ar[d]_{\Psi_{1}} 
\ar[r]^-{\phi \circ \iota} & A \ar[r]^-h & \overline{A} \\
\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}}. & & 
}
$$
Hence we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\iota^* \phi^* \Theta_2  &=& \Psi_1 \circ P(\fra) \\
&=& \Psi_1 \circ (\fra^2 - a_q(A) \fra +q)\\
&=& \Psi_3 -a_q(A) \Psi_2 + q \Psi_1.
\end{eqnarray*}

Comparing the above with (\ref{no-CL}) we obtain $\phi(\lambda) = a_q(A)$ 
which implies $\lambda = a_q(A)$ (since $a_q(A) \in {\mathbb Z}_p$) and $\gamma = q$
and the equality of the characteristic polynomials follows from the above and
Corollary \ref{char-poln} $(1)$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{gamma-rho}
Let $A$ be an elliptic curve over $S$ which is a Frobenius lift and $P(t) =
t^2 - a_q(A)t + q$ be the characteristic polynomial satisfied by the absolute
Frobenius $\overline{F}$ in $\mathrm{End}(\overline{A})$. Then
$$
\iota^*\phi^* \Theta_1 = \Psi_2 - (D\beta) \Psi_1
$$
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
For an elliptic curve $A$ we have the following diagram as follows:
$$
\xymatrix{ 
 N^{2}A \ar[r]^-{\phi\circ \iota} \ar[d]_-{\fra - \beta} & J^{1}A \ar[r] 
\ar@{.>}[dl]_{\mathfrak{g}} \ar[d]^-{\phi - \beta} & \overline{A} 
\ar[d]^-{0 } \\
 N^1A\ar[d]_{\Psi_{1}} 
\ar[r]^-{\phi \circ \iota} & A \ar[r]^-h & \overline{A} \\
\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{\mathrm{a}}. & & 
}
$$
Hence we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\iota^* \phi^* \Theta_1  &=& \Psi_1 \circ (\fra - \beta) \\
&=& \Psi_1 \circ \fra - \Psi_1 \circ \beta \\
&=& \Psi_2 - (D\beta)\Psi_1, \mbox{ by (\ref{Psi1beta})}.
\end{eqnarray*}

Comparing the above with (\ref{with-CL}) we obtain $\gamma = -(D\beta)$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{filiso}
Let $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(H)=(H,F,(H \supset V \supset \{0\}))$ and 
$\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(H')=
\newline
(H',F',(H' \supset V' \supset \{0\}))$ 
be filtered $F$-isocrystals over $K$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim_{K} H = \dim_{K} H' = 2$
\item $F(V) \ne V$ and $F'(V') \ne V'$ and
\item $p_F(t) = p_{F'}(t)=: p(t)$. 

\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(H) \simeq \mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(H')$ in the category of filtered $F$-isocrystals
over $K$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Let $p(t) = t^2 - at -b$ for some $a,b \in K$ and choose any non-zero vector
 $v \in V$. Since $F(V) \ne V$, the set $\{v, F(v)\}$ forms a $K$-basis of 
$H$. Then we have 
$$
F^{\circ 2}(v) = a F(v) + b v.
$$
Similarly, for any non-zero vector $w \in V'$ the set $\{w,F'(w)\}$ is a 
$K$-basis for $H'$ and we have
$$
F'^{\circ 2}(w) = a F'(w) + b w.
$$
Define the $K$-linear map $\Phi: H \rightarrow H'$ given by $\Phi(v):= w$ and 
$\Phi(F(v)) := F'(w)$. Then $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of $K$-vector spaces
that satisfies
$$
\xymatrix{
H \ar[d]_F \ar[r]^\Phi & H'\ar[d]^{F'}\\
H \ar[r]^\Phi & H'
}
$$
such that $\Phi(V) = V'$. Hence $\Phi:\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(H) \rightarrow \mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(H')$
is the required isomorphism of filtered $F$-isocrystals and this completes our
proof.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
We have the following two cases depending on whether $A$ admits a lift of Frobenius or not. 

(1) \textbf{\underline{Non-CL case}:} 
Consider the filtered $F$-isocrystal 
$$
\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}({\bf H}_\delta(A)_{K}) = ({\bf H}_\delta(A)_{K}, \fra^*, 
{\bf H}_\delta(A)_{K}^\bullet)
$$
where ${\bf H}_\delta(A)_{K}^\bullet$ is the filtration given by 
${\bf H}_\delta(A)_{K} \supset \bXp(A)_{K} \supset \{0\}$.
Since $A$ is non-CL, we have $\fra^*(\bXp(A)_{K}) \ne \bXp(A)_{K}$ and
the characteristic polynomial of $\fra^*$ is $p_{\fra^*}(t) = t^2 - a_q(A) t + q$.

On the other hand, consider the filtered $F$-isocrystal of the first crystalline
cohomology $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(\Hcr(A)_{K})= (\Hcr(A)_{K}, \Fc,
\Hcr(A)^\bullet_K)$ where $\Hcr(A)^\bullet_K$ is the Hodge filtration $\Hcr(A)_K 
\supset H^0(A,\Omega_A)_K \supset \{0\}$ and $\Fc$ is the crystalline Frobenius
operator on $\Hcr(A)_K$.
Since $A$ is a non-CL elliptic curve over $R$, by Theorem $3.15$ of 
\cite{BO},
$\Fc (H^0(A,\Omega_A)_{K}) \ne H^0(A,\Omega_A)_{K}$ and the characteristic
polynomial of $\Fc$ is $p_{\Fc}(t) = t^2 - a_q(A) t + q$. 

Hence by Proposition \ref{filiso} applied to $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}({\bf H}_\delta(A)_{K})$
and $\mathrm{FIso \hspace{.05cm}}(\Hcr(A)_{K})$ we obtain our required isomorphism of 
filtered $F$-isocrystals.




\vspace{.2cm}



\noindent (2) \textbf{\underline{CL case}:} 
If $\beta:A  \rightarrow A$ is the Frobenius lift map, then $D\beta$ is the induced
map on the Lie algebra $T_0A$. By (\ref{Psi1beta}) and
Lemma \ref{gamma-rho}, it follows that $-\gamma = D\beta$. Hence we have
$$
\Fc(\omega) = - \gamma \omega
$$
for all $\omega  \in H^0(A,\Omega_A)$.

On the other hand, by Theorem \ref{isoupsilon} and Theorem \ref{fra-map}(2) we 
have $\Hd(A)_K =\bXp(A)_K \stk{\Upsilon}{\simeq} H^0(A,\Omega_A)_K$ and
$\fra^*(v) = -\gamma v$ for all $v \in \Hd(A)_K$ where $\Upsilon$ is as in
Theorem \ref{isoupsilon}. 
Hence $\Upsilon$ gives us the required isomorphism of $F$-isocrystals and 
this completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
